title: How Theo built T3 Chat, the fastest AI chat app, in 5 days with a local-first architecture
summary: Theo launches T3 Chat and explains why it wins on experience rather than AI: a client-side static app shell, local-first data in IndexedDB via Dexie, and aggressive prefetching. He also covers his low-risk pricing, community-driven roadmap, and why he doesn't fear incumbents copying him.

principles.text: Differentiate on user experience, not on the underlying AI; speed and feel can be the whole product.
principles.quote: we didn't do anything interesting with the AI here what's interesting is the experience we built around it

principles.text: Go local-first and client-side when the app barely needs the server; it removes loading states and feels instant.
principles.quote: when you have an app like this where I just want to navigate click around and do things I don't need the server very often I found that building this way is really really awesome

principles.text: Show stale state instead of loading spinners; cache locally as a backup and let the UI upgrade itself.
principles.quote: there are no loading states there are just stale States

principles.text: Don't over-optimize pricing early; absorb some cost to learn what users actually want before locking tiers.
principles.quote: I didn't want to lock all of this behind us trying to guess and get a perfect pricing model I'll EAD a bit of cost if that's what it takes for us to figure out what is and isn't right

principles.text: Build because you want a better tool; being copied is fine and incumbents rarely execute well when they try.
principles.quote: I didn't build this because I want to be the only person with a chat app everyone uses I built it because I wanted a better chat app

principles.text: Run the roadmap through community feedback and reprioritize quickly when users ask for something else.
principles.quote: I have the features I want to prioritize but I will immediately delay any of them if yall have things you need more
